FieldInformation.Hint: Fixed at 60 fps for Initial D network play: always online, and in LAN / offline play once the new LAN mode is on (the online server switches it on step by step). Until then, and with the old LAN-pair settings, this setting still applies.
Uses Linear instead of nearest neighbor filtering for upscaling/downscaling textures and framebuffers. Can look nicer.

Upscale (recommended): the game runs at its native 1360x768 and the picture is scaled to ResolutionWidth x ResolutionHeight; all 2D elements stay where they belong. Game: the old behaviour, the game's own resolution code runs at that size (above 1360x768 some menus, story talk boxes and ticker clips are misplaced).

3D scene resolution when the output is above 1360x768 (Upscale). Auto: the 3D frame buffer (RenderResolutionWidth / RenderResolutionHeight) is raised to the output size while it is at its default 962x768; a value you set there always wins. Stock: keep the frame buffer fields. 1.5x / 2x: that multiple of the output (supersampling, more GPU load).

Initial D starts online by default: at every start TeknoParrot checks the online server, and with this PC registered (Account page) you get nationwide matchmaking, events and rankings. Without registration, or when the server cannot be reached, the game starts offline within seconds. Basic: nothing to set. Advanced: online server, LAN group and peers, seat, cabinet serial, the cabinet's EEPROM network record.
TPUI always selects Auto. Online when the server answers and this PC is registered; otherwise offline or LAN.

Advanced. The cabinet's own network record in the game's EEPROM (what the game's test menu shows). Online and LAN play use the Windows network of the adapter above, not these values. Leave them as they are unless a test menu needs a fixed address.
Advanced. The cabinet's address in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The subnet mask in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The gateway in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The first DNS server in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.
Advanced. The second DNS server in the game's EEPROM network record (when Dhcp is off). Not used for online or LAN play.

Advanced. LAN group of this cabinet. Empty: TeknoParrot links with the other TeknoParrot PCs of your network after you confirm the link once. A name (the same on every cabinet of one store) separates stores that share a network, counts as the confirmation, and allows LAN play on a network Windows marks as Public. Only PCs with the same group and the same game link.

Advanced. Extra addresses to look for, separated by commas. Normally empty: TeknoParrot finds the other PCs by itself. Needed on networks that do not pass broadcasts (Tailscale and similar), and for a PC on another subnet.
Advanced. The name the other PCs show for this one. Empty = the Windows computer name. It is the only thing this PC puts on the network before a link.

Advanced. Seat of this cabinet in its store. AUTO (recommended): TeknoParrot assigns the seat itself when it finds another TeknoParrot PC on your network, and SINGLE when it finds none. SINGLE: never seated. A1..D2: a fixed seat (tournaments, cabinets that must keep their place). A seat two PCs claim at once sends the later one to SINGLE.

Advanced. Optional cabinet serial (letters/digits, the first 11 are sent to ALL.Net). Empty = a stable serial generated from this PC. Set it only when two PCs would otherwise get the same serial (cloned or imaged installs). Two online game instances on one PC are not supported. Online play only. A registered PC uses its Online ID instead on the official server.

Hidden: managed on the Account page (Initial D Online). Your Initial D Online PCB ID (AALG-...), filled in by TeknoParrotUI from your teknoparrot.com account. Used only for online play on the official server; offline and LAN play ignore it. One PC per account.

Hidden: managed on the Account page (Initial D Online). The secret that belongs to OnlineID (43 characters). Keep it private: it lets anyone play as you. Used only for online play on the official server.
Debug: log every server box packet / store DB command and more to TeknoParrot\id5online.log in the game folder.
Debug: log the game's network state (seqInitNetwork, store link, DB/match alive, ALL.Net auth) once per second to TeknoParrot\id5online.log.

Online only: predict the opponent's car from each packet's age so it is shown where it really is (100-300 ms internet latency: position error p95 about 3-7 m instead of 27-50 m). Also stops the opponent running far ahead after a crash.
Online only: send your car state every N frames. 1 = 60 Hz (recommended with LagComp, about 8.4 kB/s), 6 = stock 10 Hz.
Text chat with your rival in online matches (F2 type, Enter send, Esc close, Ctrl+1..4 quick phrases, /mute). Goes through the TeknoParrot server; nothing is stored.
Voice chat in online matches, through the server you play on (not stored, not recorded). talk uses your microphone (a headset is advised; no echo cancelling); F3: talk + listen -> listen only -> off.
Optional push-to-talk key; empty = voice activation.
